prompt:
data/ has 30 customer export files, customers-01.json to customers-30.json. Clean all 30 files in place (same names, same folder) following the rules below. Write a script to do it and run it on every file; the files are too many and too messy to edit by hand.

File layout: each file is a JSON object with the top level keys source, exportedAt, count and customers (in a different order from file to file). Keep the top level keys in the order they have in the file. Leave source and exportedAt as they are. Set count to the number of customers after cleaning. Only customers is cleaned otherwise. Some files start with a UTF-8 byte order mark and some use CRLF line endings; the output has neither. A customer has the keys id, name, email, phone, signup, country, tags and last_login (some customers lack last_login), plus up to four keys that are dropped.

Steps for each file, in this order:
1. Clean each customer. Remove the keys internal_score, notes, ssn_last4 and debug. name: remove spaces and tabs at both ends and replace every run of spaces and tabs inside with one space. email: remove spaces at both ends and make it lower case. country: remove spaces at both ends and make it upper case. tags: for each tag remove spaces at both ends and make it lower case, drop empty tags, and remove repeats keeping the first one. last_login is not changed. A key that is missing stays missing.
2. phone: if the key is present, the new value is a string in the form `+1 AAA-BBB-CCCC` or null. First remove an extension: everything from the first `x` or `ext` (any letter case) to the end of the value. Then keep only the digits. If that is 10 digits, or 11 digits that start with 1, use the last 10 digits as AAABBBCCCC. Anything else (including an empty or blank value, or null) becomes null.
3. signup: if the key is present, the new value is a date written as YYYY-MM-DD or null. The accepted input formats are `YYYY-MM-DD`, `M/D/YYYY` (month first, one or two digits for month and day), `D.M.YYYY` (day first, dots, one or two digits) and `Mon D, YYYY` where Mon is one of Jan Feb Mar Apr May Jun Jul Aug Sep Oct Nov Dec and D has one or two digits. The year always has 4 digits. Spaces around the whole value are ignored. A value in any other format, or one that is not a real calendar date (for example 31.02.2021, 13/01/2021 or 29.02.2021), becomes null. Leap years count.
4. Remove every customer whose cleaned email is missing, null or empty.
5. Merge duplicates. Customers are duplicates when their cleaned emails are exactly equal. Each group becomes one customer. Its id is the id of the duplicate that comes first in the file. Its tags are the union of all the duplicates' cleaned tags in the order first seen. For every other key, use the value from the last duplicate (in file order) whose cleaned value is not missing, not null and not an empty string. If no duplicate has such a value, use the first duplicate's cleaned value, so null stays null and a missing key stays missing. Emails that differ in any way other than letter case or surrounding spaces (for example a +tag, or another domain) are different customers.
6. Sort the customers by id, ascending as numbers.
7. Write each customer with its keys in this order: id, name, email, phone, signup, country, tags, last_login. Keys that are missing are left out.

Output format of every file: JSON with 2 space indentation, LF line endings, one newline at the end of the file, and non ASCII characters written as themselves (not as backslash u escapes such as \u00e9).
